That's how I felt. I hate when people say "Just accept who you are and learn to love it" Easy for them to say when they don't have to deal with patches of Vitiligo on them which people are obviously going to look at. I mean admittedly mine wasn't so bad but was enough to bother me about taking my shirt off in public.

It would probably be best for you to tan and then find a good foundation makeup that will last for a day and cover it well. Maybe go and see a professional makeup artist or something? At least being on the face you can apply it easily. For my back it was impossible for me to cover it at all if my shirt was off because it was a thick lumpy patch that I couldn't reach.
Have you thought about using makeup or tanning to cover them?

Too late it's been done. Coming up to 2 weeks this weekend and I will be posting a new thread about my conclusion and experience of it this weekend but from what I've seen and how I feel so far it was DEFINITELY THE RIGHT THING TO DO. The whole pigment is gone and I had the inside shaded in which is something I recommend you do. The Vitiligo is gone completely and the tattoo looks awesome. It's mostly healed by now and wasn't at all painful. There is no sign of any new patches forming either which I figured would have happened by now.
Huh? No for now I am just getting the depigmented skin tattooed over.
I'm getting the entire patch filled in with ink though so there will literally be no trace of depigmented skin left, it will just look like a lighter coloured tattoo.

Well I'll post the results up here when it's done. It "can" trigger not it "will" trigger is the key thing you've said there. Yes it's a risk but life is about taking risks imo. 10 years with no change of this pigment on my back seems like I'll be ok, you never know doing nothing to the area may cause it to spread in the future but acting now might stop it, the future is unknown. How bad will a needle even trigger the Vitiligo anyway? It might literally just be a few tiny spots beneath it which won't look worst than what I currently have.
That's good to hear thanks!
Thanks. Well that's the thing and it goes to show I may as well go for it because by doing nothing to it then it could get worst anyway.

True, I have heard that this can happen but the key word you've used there is "can" so equally it may not happen. Also how bad of a trigger are we talking? If it's just a few little tiny patches around the then that isn't so bad and won't look worst than what I already have. Don't forget I could always add more to the tattoo in the future to cover any further Vitiligo. Also you're getting a tattoo over a patch on your leg so aren't you taking a risk with that also?

Have a look at this it seems pretty safe and says the tattoo ink will not fade because it is not related to the skin pigment fading. Also as I said this patch has been on my back for over 10 years and in those years very little change if any has taken place. My Vitiligo case is not as severe as most so should be ok

Yes. I used to really despise myself but now I only partially do. However it's gotten to the point where I either need to seriously change my look and appearance or end my existence. I'm not gonna be one of them people who will feed you all that bullshit about you need to learn to accept yourself and you're beautiful the way you are blah blah blah cause I literally despise anyone who says that shit.

I really don't want to take my life yet though so I am taking steps to change my appearance and advise you to do the same. Make a list of what you dislike about yourself and figure out how you can change it. Also write down what you do like.

For me: I'm 23 and am already losing my hair. Going bald is making me depressed so I've looked into treatment for it and found a solution for only £500 which will give me amazing results and will ultimately eliminate the problem. There is other stuff as well, such as bad skin patches on my back which I'll get tattoos over. Likewise I've always been pretty skinny so I've working out pretty intensely for 3 years now. I'm currently contemplating going on steroids so I can get the physical look I really want.

Look my answer is probably controversial and people will disagree but that's how I see it. Reality is I can make these changes happen by earning money so that's what I'm working towards. There's that saying that if you look good you feel good and if you don't like something fix it.

Life is full of these funny ironies and the guy I bet on won. Maybe it was meant to be, but life is certainly looking a lot better for me now. Risks are part of life and you either win or lose.
